main_text.l: Cur aut quomodo utile & necessarium?
Quia ideo institutum est à Deo, primùm, ne
homo fit solus, sed habeat sociam & adjutri-
cem conjunctam in tota vita, nec solùm in
procreatione, sed etiam in educatione libe-
rorum, in regenda familia, in parandis & tu-
endis rebus ad hanc vitam necessariis, ut par-
tem laborum & molestiarum sustineat, &
ut omnis fortunæ sociam, & quasi solatium
& levamen multarum miseriarum hujus æ-
rumnosæ vitæ habeat. Genef.2. Ecclef. 4.9.
Neque enim in ærumnis remedium ullum
suavius & dulcius est, quàm præsentia &
confociatio piæ & prudentis conjugis: Sic-
uti & Proverb.31. dicitur: Cui contigit pro-
ba uxor, ea præstat gemmis, confidit ea cor
mariti, & res familiaris non deficiet. Et Ec-
cles.26. Mulier comis exhilarat maritum: &
cùm humaniter eum tractat, recreat cor e-
jus. Item cap.37. Mulier formosa exhilarat
maritum suum. Et cap.40. Ut amicus com-
modè congruat cum amico, vir tamen & u-
xor concordes utriq; præferendi sunt. Hinc
Augustinus de bono Conjugali cap.3. ait:
Quod (bonum conjugii bonum) mihi non
videtur propter solam filiorum procreatio-
nem, sed propter ipsam naturalem in diver-
so sexu societatem. Alioqui non jam dicere-
tur conjugium in senibus, præsertim si vel a-
mississent filios, vel minimè genuissent. Nunc
verò in bono licet annoso conjugio, etsi e-

page.notes: Genef. and Ecclef. are printed with long-s forms; transcribed as Genes. and Eccles. per the rule on long s, with the printed forms kept in the text where they appear as abbreviations. Doubtful readings: "Alioqui" (accent unclear), "amississent" (the ss ligature is hard to read), "Genef.2." and "Eccles." as printed. Margin fragments at the far right edge are cut off and unreadable; they are not transcribed. The page number reads 451 as printed; the final digit is small and somewhat doubtful.
